item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love these logs. I tend to enjoy overexplained SCPs though, but it seems like others like it too.

My one problem here, and with many other pages involving D-class dialogue, is that they sound way too clinical and formal at times. Certainly a far cry from the staff's dialogue, but I would think that people scooped up out of death row or hobos off the streets wouldn't sound so…educated, and disciplined. I do realize that D-class are more of an in-universe convenience than anything, but I recently read the Cabinet Labyrinth (or whatever it's called) just a little ways back from this one in the list and its logs gave each D-class a small description including a bit of background and temperament. It was fantastic, and I think other articles could benefit from similar tidbits.

All that rant aside, I'm one that always sees room for improvement and I tend to emphasize that more than what I like about something. I could probably write many times more regarding what I like about this SCP. And with that, I'll step off my soapbox.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So, through this accelerated evolutionary set up, where more complicated organisms can simply manifest with more SCP-440, with a few thousand kiloliters of this stuff, we might see more intelligent life.

Which would end horribly. It always does.

I like it.

item.content:encoded:
Not the first, 093 springs to mind as one where D-Class came back alive. Same with that one stairwell.

I do not think it is coincidence that those were also great SCPs. Having some people survive makes it more tense than letting people safely assume everyone is doomed ahead of time.
